articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Kettle Hill
articles.deck: Residents of Kettle Hill filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The Kettle Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Council Delays Vote on Mulberry Avenue Streetlight Upgrade
articles.deck: The vote came after 12 residents spoke at Saturday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 12 weeks once it starts in July. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Councilmember Gloria Baptiste asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Bellwood said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Letter: The Neighborhood Watch Sign Program on Ridge Lane Needs Attention
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the October meeting.
To the editor: I have lived on Ridge Lane for 20 years, and I want to say what a difference the Cedar Hollow Garden Club has made.
Please keep the neighborhood watch sign program in the budget. Many of us on Ridge Lane use it every week. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Arthur Mahoney, Tannery Flats

articles.title: Then & Now: Carver Lane in 1998 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1998 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Carver Lane from the corner of Nash Drive. Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
